name: Trap Bar Deadlift
notes: Low-dose strength-retention touch, D-21 to D-8 only, and only for fighters who already train the trap-bar deadlift (familiarity_required): never introduce it cold in the final stretch. Keep it non-grinding, no failure, no back-off volume, no soreness target; stop on any bar-speed or quality loss. The taper dose caps thin sets/reps as the fight nears. Not for D-7 or later.

name: Med Ball Scoop Toss
notes: Use a light medicine ball and full rest; drive from the hips and transfer force through the torso without chasing fatigue.

name: Landmine Press → Med Ball Chest Pass
Hang Power Clean
notes: Technical Olympic-lift option for experienced MMA and wrestling athletes during GPP only; use low-volume, crisp reps.

name: Trap Bar Jump
notes: Use a light load and full recovery; prioritize jump height and bar speed over load.

name: Jump Squat
notes: Use bodyweight or a very light load for 3-5 sets of 3 reps with full rest; stop when jump height drops.

name: Kettlebell Swing
notes: Explosive hip-hinge option for repeated alactic power; end the set when snap speed slows.

name: Landmine Push Press
notes: Use a split stance, light-to-moderate load, and full rest; drive through the floor and finish fast.

name: Single-Leg Balance (Eyes Closed)
notes: Progress by adding head turns or unstable surface

name: Tandem Gait Walk (Heel-to-Toe)
notes: Add backward walking for progression

name: Bosu Ball Mini-Squats
notes: Keep squats shallow (30° knee bend)

name: Foam Pad Alphabet Tracing
notes: Trace letters with toes while standing on one leg

name: Reactive Band Taps (Partner)
notes: Partner gently tugs band in random directions during single-leg stance

name: Single-Leg Medicine Ball Chest Push Jump
Atlas Stone Load Isometric (120% max stone @ lap)
KB Suitcase Carry
pro_tip: Hold KB opposite side of working leg to maximize oblique engagement - mimics sprawl recovery mechanics
combat_carryover: Develops clinch grip endurance and cross-body power transfer for hooks

name: Pallof Press Iso (Against Resistance)
notes: Low-cost anti-rotation trunk-stability support (overcoming isometric). Keep the dose tiny and intent moderate; not a maximal-strength anchor.

name: Bird Dog Hold
notes: From quadruped, reach opposite arm and leg with trunk square. Stop on quality drop.

name: Suitcase Carry Holds
notes: Low-cost grip/anti-rotation trunk support, not a maximal-strength anchor. Use only when grip/trunk work fits the athlete; keep totals tiny (2-3 short holds per side) and never chase grip or trunk fatigue. Shrink the dose from D-7 inward.

name: Kettlebell Suitcase Carry Hold
notes: Low-cost grip/anti-rotation trunk support, not a maximal-strength anchor. Use only when grip/trunk work fits the athlete; keep totals tiny (2-3 short holds per side) and never chase grip or trunk fatigue. Shrink the dose from D-7 inward.

name: Isometric Mid-Thigh Pull
contraindications: skip when pins or trap bar are unavailable
avoid if maximal pulling intent irritates the low back
notes: Late-camp force-preservation pull from a fixed mid-thigh position; low-eccentric, low-soreness neural/max-force maintenance. Usable through D-7 at very low dose (2-3 x 3-5s, full rest, maximal intent). Keep total volume tiny. Not for D-6 or later.

name: Trap-Bar Pin Pull Isometric
contraindications: skip when pins or trap bar are unavailable
avoid if aggressive brace work spikes blood pressure during the cut
notes: 2–3x4–6s, full setup and full rest. Prioritise D-13; only use on D-7 if dose stays very low. Not for D-3 or D-1.

name: Punch-Specific Max Isometric Hold
contraindications: avoid if shoulder or wrist pain spikes when bracing against the bag
notes: Maximal-strength maintenance / neural work: no eccentric, no landing, low soreness. D-13 to D-8: 2-3 x 3-5s per side with full rest; shrink to 1-2 short holds per side through D-7 and D-6/D-5. Keep out of D-4 to D-1. Not for D-1: requires equipment.

name: Overcoming Split-Squat Isometric
contraindications: skip if front-knee irritation increases with split-stance pressure
notes: 2-3 x 5-10s per leg with full rest. Use in D-13 to D-8 only as a tiny exposure when needed; not for D-1: requires bands.

name: Staggered-Stance Medicine-Ball Punch Throw
contraindications: skip if trunk rotation is currently symptom-limited
notes: Low-volume punch throw from a fight stance. Keep it crisp, chest-height, and never chase fatigue.

name: Towel/Gi Row Isometric Hold
contraindications: skip if elbow tendons are already flared by heavy gripping
notes: Short-duration towel or gi row hold for grip and upper-back tension with almost no soreness cost.

name: Band-Resisted Jab-Cross Primer
contraindications: skip if shoulder speed drops or punching mechanics feel noisy
notes: Micro-dose band primer for crisp jab-cross sequencing. Keep reps low, fast, and fully recovered.

name: Adductor Squeeze Isometric
contraindications: skip if adductor squeeze increases groin pain beyond a mild awareness
notes: Gentle but high-value groin and pelvis tension touch that survives hard cuts and the final days before fighting.

name: Split-Stance Wall-Drive Isometric
notes: 2-3 x 5-8s per side with full reset. Not for D-1: requires equipment.

name: Half-Kneeling Medicine-Ball Punch Throw
notes: Low-volume punch throw: 2-3 x 3 per side with full rest early, shrinking to 1-2 crisp throws as the fight nears. Micro-dose only on D-7, D-6/D-5, D-4 and D-2; med-ball throws are pulled entirely on D-3 and D-1 by the final-sharpening rules.

name: Seated Medicine-Ball Punch Throw
notes: 2-3 x 3 throws with full rest, using progressively smaller micro-doses (down to 1-2 crisp throws) as the fight approaches. Micro-dose only on D-7, D-6/D-5, D-4 and D-2; med-ball throws are pulled entirely on D-3 and D-1 by the final-sharpening rules.

name: Landmine Split-Stance Punch Press
contraindications: avoid if shoulder symptoms are active
notes: 2-3 x 3 per side with full rest. Keep very light and avoid final-day use.

name: Tempo Push-Up (3-1-1)
notes: Equipment-free horizontal press. Lower for 3 seconds, pause 1 second just above the floor, press up in 1 second with a rigid plank from head to heels. Stop the set when the hips sag or the tempo breaks. Progress by elevating the feet; regress by raising the hands onto a sturdy surface.

name: Feet-Elevated Push-Up
notes: Feet on a step, chair or bed edge so more bodyweight loads the press. Hands under the shoulders, ribs down, chest to just above the floor on every rep. Stop when the hips pike or the lockout softens. Regress to a floor push-up.

name: Pike Push-Up
notes: Equipment-free overhead press. Hips high in an inverted V, lower the crown of the head toward the floor between the hands, then press back up. Keep elbows about 45 degrees from the body. Skip with any shoulder pain overhead; regress by keeping the hands on a raised surface.

name: Band Bent-Over Row
notes: Stand on the band, bend at the hips to a flat back, and row both handles to the lower ribs. Pause 1 second with the shoulder blades back, lower under control. Choose a band that makes the last two reps of each set hard but clean; shorten the band or double it to progress.

name: Half-Kneeling Single-Arm Band Row
notes: Anchor the band at chest height. Half-kneeling with the working-side knee down, row one handle to the ribs without letting the torso rotate toward the band. Pause 1 second, lower slowly, finish all reps on one side, then change sides.

name: Split Squat (Bodyweight Tempo 3-1-1)
notes: Equipment-free unilateral leg strength. Long split stance, lower for 3 seconds until the back knee hovers just above the floor, pause 1 second, drive up through the front foot. Finish all reps on one leg, then change legs. Progress by elevating the rear foot on a step; regress by shortening the range.
